key_insight: Mesoscale neural operators learn nonlocal constitutive laws from molecular dynamics while preserving strain energy density and fracture energy across horizon rescaling.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables continuum fracture simulations on much larger domains and coarser grids than atomistic simulations can afford.
method: Learn a nonlocal kernel and nonlinear constitutive relation from MD loading and displacement data.
Normalize the kernel to preserve strain energy density under horizon rescaling.
Rescale critical bond stretch to maintain consistent fracture energy across scales.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests support model recovery; MD-based tests report energy metrics within 3% and out-of-distribution peak forces within 6%, plus a fracture demonstration on a plate with 4,000× the training-specimen area.
watch_item: The reported tests do not establish generalization to other materials or loading regimes; broader validation is needed before engineering deployment.
paper_title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
